| `dunning_config.adaptive_timing` | `boolean` | no | Smart mode only. Times each retry by why the payment failed instead of using the retry offsets: gateway and network faults retry within hours (4h, 1 day, 3 days), insufficient funds retries on the next likely payday (the 1st, 15th or last day of the month, up to 4 times), and generic declines retry 2, 3 and 4 days apart, then the invoice parks (park_hard_declines on) or reaches the final action. Day-based retries land at 10:00 local to the card's issuing country when it is known (the business's timezone otherwise), and every retry stays within 30 days of the due date and inside dunning_period_days. Mandate debits (UPI, e-NACH, card mandates) and other decline codes keep the retry offsets. The timings are heuristics, not card-network requirements. Default false. |

A currency with no entry has no minimum. Default {} (no minimum). |
| `dunning_config.park_hard_declines` | `boolean` | no | Smart mode, plus fixed mode's mandate and gateway-limit refusals. true parks a hard-recoverable decline (expired or invalid card, authentication required, mandate refusals, and a generic decline after 4 failed attempts): no automatic retries, reminder emails, then one last attempt and the final action at the end of the dunning period (30 days after it parks when none is set). false (default) retries those declines on the schedule like any other and applies the final action when it runs out; with no dunning_period_days, card declines keep a 30-day window. | `reminder_config.renewal_yearly` | `array of integer` | no | Days before a renewal on which to send the renewal reminder, for yearly or longer terms. |
| `reminder_config.cancellation` | `array of integer` | no | Days before a scheduled cancellation on which to send the cancellation reminder. |
| `reminder_config.card_expiring` | `string | array of integer` | no | `expiry_month` (default): `payment_source_expiring` mails the customer when the card enters its expiry month. A list of lead days instead sends `payment_source_expiry_reminder` (and the `card_expiring` email) on each day before the card expires. `payment_source_expiring` still fires once, without the email. |
| `reminder_config.payment_due` | `array of integer` | no | Days before the due date of an open invoice that is not collected automatically: `invoice_payment_due_reminder`. [] (default) is off. |
| `reminder_config.pause` | `array of integer` | no | Days before a scheduled pause: `subscription_pause_reminder`. [] (default) is off. |
| `reminder_config.resume` | `array of integer` | no | Days before a scheduled resume: `subscription_resume_reminder`. [] (default) is off. |
| `checkout_field_config` | `object` | no | Which checkout fields show, hide, or are required. Absent keys resolve to defaults that are not uniform: billing.line1, billing.city, billing.state_code, billing.postal_code and billing.country are mandatory, everything else shows, and invoice.po_number is hidden (and still gated by storefront_config.collect_po_number). A mandatory region or postal code applies only where the country has one. billing.country cannot be hide (400). While the business has a live tax region, billing.country must stay mandatory, and while it has a GST region billing.state_code must too (400 otherwise; see `address_field_locks`). Making billing.postal_code mandatory is also the AVS/ZIP-verification control, since AVS is checked gateway-side. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.first_name` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's first name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.last_name` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's last name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.email` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's email. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.phone` | `string` | no | The business's phone number. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.company` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the customer's company. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.customer.tax_registration_number` | `string` | no | The business's tax registration number. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.line1` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 1. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.line2` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 2. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.line3` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires address line 3. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.city` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the city. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.state` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the state name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.state_code` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the state code. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.postal_code` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires the postal code. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.billing.country` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows or requires the country. One of `show`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.invoice.po_number` | `string` | no | Whether checkout shows, hides or requires a purchase order number. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `checkout_field_config.shipping.address` | `string` | no | Whether checkout collects a shipping address. hide (the default) collects none; show lets the buyer add one; mandatory requires one. The address goes into the customer's shipping address book as the default, and a new subscription ships to it. Tax still uses the billing address. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`. |
| `portal_field_config` | `object` | no | Which billing-detail fields the buyer portal shows, hides, requires, or shows read-only. Absent keys resolve to defaults: customer.first_name, customer.phone, billing.line1, billing.city, billing.state_code, billing.postal_code and billing.country are mandatory, everything else shows. A portal save keeps the stored value of every hide or read_only key; billing.state and billing.state_code are one region, kept only when both are hide or read_only. billing.country cannot be hide (400). The tax rules of checkout_field_config apply here too. |
| `portal_field_config.customer.first_name` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's first name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.customer.last_name` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's last name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.customer.phone` | `string` | no | The business's phone number. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.customer.company` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the customer's company. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.customer.tax_registration_number` | `string` | no | The business's tax registration number. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.line1` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 1. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.line2` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 2. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.line3` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks address line 3. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.city` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the city. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.state` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the state name. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.state_code` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the state code. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.postal_code` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, hides, requires or locks the postal code. One of `show`, `hide`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `portal_field_config.billing.country` | `string` | no | Whether the portal shows, requires or locks the country. One of `show`, `mandatory`, `read_only`. |
| `chargeback_config` | `object` | no | What a chargeback does to the invoice and the subscription. Absent keys resolve to record-only, which is the behaviour before this field existed. The invoice action applies to a LOST dispute only and its one value raises a DOCUMENTARY credit note (no ledger entries — the dispute's own dispute_losses posting remains the accounting treatment). A "mark invoice Not Paid" action is not offered: it would resurrect accounts_receivable with no matching ledger entry. |
| `chargeback_config.on_lost_invoice` | `string` | no | What happens to the invoice when a dispute is lost. One of `credit_note`, `no_action`. |
| `chargeback_config.on_initiated_subscription` | `string` | no | What happens to the subscription when a dispute starts. One of `cancel_immediately`, `cancel_end_of_term`, `pause_indefinitely`, `pause_end_of_term`, `no_action`. |
| `chargeback_config.on_lost_subscription` | `string` | no | What happens to the subscription when a dispute is lost. One of `cancel_immediately`, `cancel_end_of_term`, `pause_indefinitely`, `pause_end_of_term`, `no_action`. |
| `chargeback_config.cascade_to_other_subscriptions` | `boolean` | no | Whether the subscription action also applies to the customer's other subscriptions. |
| `chargeback_config.stop_collecting_all` | `boolean` | no | Whether to stop collecting on all the customer's invoices. |
| `vies_validation_enabled` | `boolean` | no | Validate customer VAT numbers against VIES. TRUE means validate — stated positively so the field reads correctly at its call sites. The switch exists because VIES is third-party and goes down. |
| `storefront_config` | `object` | no | What the checkout and self-serve portal do. Absent keys resolve to today's behaviour. The two URLs are the fallback for the checkout mint, which requires them per call when no default is set; a call with neither is still refused. |
| `storefront_config.hide_zero_value_lines` | `boolean` | no | Whether lines with a zero value are hidden. |
| `storefront_config.collect_po_number` | `boolean` | no | Whether checkout asks for a purchase order number. |
| `storefront_config.default_return_url` | `string` | no | The URL checkout returns to after a payment, when the request has none. |
| `storefront_config.default_cancel_url` | `string` | no | The URL checkout returns to after a cancel, when the request has none. |
| `storefront_config.allow_invoice_download` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer download an invoice PDF from the portal? Default true. |
| `storefront_config.allow_invoice_payment` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer pay an unpaid invoice from the portal? Default true. Turning it off removes the buyer's own payment path only — the engine still collects on its schedule and dunning still runs. |
| `storefront_config.allow_remove_payment_method` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer remove a stored payment method? Default true. Turn it off where a live mandate depends on the instrument. |
| `storefront_config.allow_cancel_subscription` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer cancel their own subscription from the portal? Default FALSE — the route is new, so granting it is the change. |
| `storefront_config.allow_pause_resume` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer pause AND resume their own subscription? Default false. One key for both directions — offering pause without resume would trap a buyer. Pause uses the business's own pause defaults. |
| `storefront_config.allow_skip_renewal` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer skip an upcoming renewal from the portal? Default false. Capped by `skip_renewal_limit`. |
| `storefront_config.skip_renewal_limit` | `integer` | no | Most renewals a buyer may skip in 12 months. Default 3. Operators are not capped. |
| `storefront_config.portal_show_usage` | `boolean` | no | Show the buyer the usage so far on each metered subscription in the portal. Default true. |
| `storefront_config.portal_show_usage_projection` | `boolean` | no | Also show the projected usage at the end of the billing window. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.allow_reactivate` | `boolean` | no | May a buyer undo a pending cancellation? Default false. Covers a subscription still active with cancel_at_period_end; an already-cancelled one is refused, because restarting it bills a new period. |
| `storefront_config.cancel_timing` | `string` | no | When a buyer-initiated cancellation takes effect. Default `end_of_term`. The merchant's choice, not the buyer's — it is not accepted as a request parameter. Money handling comes from the business's own cancellation defaults, so a buyer cancel settles identically to an operator cancel. One of `immediately`, `end_of_term`. |
| `storefront_config.portal_link_error_html` | `string` | no | Rich text the customer portal shows when a buyer cannot get in — an expired, used, revoked or unknown link, or an ended session. Allowed markup: p, br, b, strong, i, em, u, h1, h2, ul, ol, li and a (http, https or mailto); anything else is stripped on read. Null keeps the default copy. |
| `storefront_config.one_time_save_payment_method` | `string` | no | Whether a one-time purchase keeps the buyer's payment method for later purchases. `ask` (the default) lets the buyer decide. One of `never`, `always`, `ask`. |
| `storefront_config.checkout_layout` | `string` | no | Hosted checkout layout. `one_page` shows details and payment together; `steps` shows them one after another. Default `steps`; new businesses start with `one_page`. One of `steps`, `one_page`. |
| `storefront_config.wallets_first` | `boolean` | no | Show Apple Pay and Google Pay above the form when the buyer's device and the payment gateway support them. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.recurring_consent` | `boolean` | no | The buyer must agree to the recurring charge (amount and period) before paying. Default false. The agreement is recorded. |
| `storefront_config.require_terms` | `boolean` | no | The buyer must accept the terms (and the privacy policy when set). Has no effect until terms_url is set. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.terms_url` | `string` | no | Terms of service link shown at checkout (http or https). |
| `storefront_config.privacy_url` | `string` | no | Privacy policy link shown at checkout (http or https). |
| `storefront_config.marketing_consent` | `boolean` | no | Offer an optional marketing opt-in at checkout. The answer is stored on the customer. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.bot_check_after_failures` | `integer` | no | Ask for a bot check after this many failed payments from one IP address in 24 hours. Null (the default) turns it off. |
| `storefront_config.allow_plan_changes` | `boolean` | no | Customers can change plan, seats and add-ons in the portal. Which plans and add-ons they see is each product's enabled_in_portal. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.seat_changes` | `string` | no | Seat (per-unit plan quantity) changes in the portal. Default `off`. One of `off`, `increase`, `both`. |
| `storefront_config.seat_min` | `integer` | no | The seat min. |
| `storefront_config.seat_max` | `integer` | no | The seat max. |
| `storefront_config.allow_addon_changes` | `boolean` | no | Customers can add or remove add-ons in the portal. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.shorter_period` | `string` | no | A move to a shorter billing period (yearly to monthly) in the portal. Default `always`. One of `always`, `never`, `after_12_months`. |
| `storefront_config.charge_upgrade` | `string` | no | When a portal upgrade is invoiced. `business_default` (the default) follows unbilled_charges_config.on_change. One of `business_default`, `now`, `next_invoice`. |
| `storefront_config.change_statuses` | `array of string` | no | Subscription statuses that may change in the portal. Default active and in_trial. |
| `storefront_config.allow_cancel_scheduled_change` | `boolean` | no | Customers can withdraw a plan change scheduled for the end of the term. Default true. |
| `storefront_config.cancel_reason` | `string` | no | Ask for a cancel reason in the portal (the business's cancel reason codes). Default `optional`. One of `off`, `optional`, `required`. |
| `storefront_config.retention_pause` | `boolean` | no | Offer a pause before the customer cancels. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.retention_pause_months` | `integer` | no | Length of the offered pause in months; null = no end date. Default 3. |
| `storefront_config.retention_pause_choice` | `boolean` | no | The customer picks 1 to retention_pause_months months. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.retention_downgrade_price` | `string` | no | Offer a move to this cheaper plan price (price id) before the customer cancels. Null = no offer. |
| `storefront_config.retention_coupon` | `string` | no | Offer this coupon code before the customer cancels. Null = no offer. |
| `storefront_config.retention_contact_url` | `string` | no | Offer a link to contact you before the customer cancels. Null = no offer. |
| `storefront_config.retention_offer_once` | `boolean` | no | A customer who took an offer before is not offered one again. Default true. |
| `storefront_config.portal_email_code` | `boolean` | no | The signed-out portal lets a customer sign in with a code sent to their email. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.portal_link_hours` | `integer` | no | How long a portal link minted through the API can be opened, in hours. Null = 1 hour. |
| `storefront_config.portal_email_link_days` | `integer` | no | How long a portal link in an email can be opened, in days. Null = 5 days. |
| `storefront_config.portal_session_hours` | `integer` | no | How long a customer stays signed in to the portal, in hours. Null = 72 hours. |
| `storefront_config.portal_hide_cancelled_subscriptions` | `boolean` | no | The portal does not list cancelled subscriptions. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.portal_hide_zero_invoices` | `boolean` | no | The portal does not list invoices with a zero total. An invoice with an amount due always shows. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.portal_hide_voided_invoices` | `boolean` | no | The portal does not list voided invoices. Default false. |
| `storefront_config.portal_actions` | `object` | no | Which tasks a portal link may open on. Each defaults to true; false makes such a link open the portal home. |
| `storefront_config.portal_return_url` | `string` | no | https only. Where the portal's back link goes. Null = default_return_url. A portal link's own redirect_url wins. |
| `default_tax_behavior` | `string` | no | Default price type new prices inherit One of `exclusive`, `inclusive`. |
| `tax_behavior_by_currency` | `object` | no | Price type per currency, as `{"INR": "inclusive"}`. A new price created without `tax_behavior` takes its currency's value. Sent whole; null removes every value. |
| `seller_tax_ids` | `object` | no | Your tax registration per destination country, keyed by ISO 3166-1 code (GB, not UK; GR, not EL), as `{"DE": "DE123456789"}`. An invoice to a customer in that country prints it in place of the business tax ID. Sent whole; null removes every value. |
| `tax_rounding` | `string` | no | `per_invoice_total` (default) rounds each tax once on the invoice total. `per_line` rounds the tax on each line and adds the lines. One of `per_invoice_total`, `per_line`. |
| `anchor_granularity` | `string` | no | Where a term starts: the exact creation instant, or floored to start-of-day in the business timezone (day-anchored businesses also report term ends inclusively, …T23:59:59) One of `instant`, `day`. |
| `proration_granularity` | `string` | no | How mid-term credits/charges are measured: by elapsed time, or by whole billing days. Legal pairs are instant+exact (millisecond-based), instant+whole_day (day-based) and day+whole_day (day-based with midnight-aligned terms) One of `exact`, `whole_day`. |
| `email_config` | `object` | no | Customer-facing billing emails; null disables all sending |
| `email_config.enabled` | `boolean` | no | Whether the business sends billing emails. |
| `email_config.fromName` | `string` | no | The From name on billing emails. |
| `email_config.fromAddress` | `string` | no | Envelope From; null uses the deployment default. |
| `email_config.replyTo` | `string` | no | Null sends NO Reply-To header, so replies go to the From address. There is no fallback to the business support email. |
| `email_config.cc` | `array of string` | no | Copied on every send and VISIBLE to the customer. Max 10. |
| `email_config.bcc` | `array of string` | no | Copied on every send and hidden from the customer — the usual place for an internal archive box. Max 10. |
| `email_config.subjectPrefix` | `string` | no | Prepended to every rendered subject, e.g. "[Fernhill]". Applied at send time, so email_messages.subject keeps the unprefixed rendered subject. |
| `email_config.footerNote` | `string` | no | The business footer: ends every email that has no footer of its own. Template syntax, limited to the variables every email has (businessName, customerName, portalUrl). Null uses the built-in footer. |
| `email_config.attachments` | `object` | no | Per-email attachment rules, keyed by email type. Only types about a document take effect: invoice_issued, invoice_overdue, invoice_sent, payment_receipt, payment_failed, payment_authentication_required (the invoice PDF) and credit_note_issued, credit_note_applied, credit_note_sent (the credit note PDF). An absent type attaches the PDF and skips nothing. `skipZeroPdf` applies to invoice_issued and invoice_sent only; `skipZeroSend` to invoice_issued only. The PDF is rendered when the email is sent. |
| `email_config.types` | `object` | no | Per-email-type override; absent type inherits `enabled` |
| `email_config.attachReceiptPdf` | `boolean` | no | Attach the numbered receipt PDF to the payment confirmation email. Default false. |
| `email_config.linkTarget` | `string` | no | Where the links and the button in billing emails go. `portal` (default): a signed-in link to the hosted billing portal. `merchant_url`: `merchantUrl`, as it is, with no portal session. One of `portal`, `merchant_url`. |
| `email_config.merchantUrl` | `string` | no | An http(s) URL. Required when `linkTarget` is `merchant_url`. Kept when you change the target back to `portal`. |
| `team_alerts_config` | `object` | no | Mail to your own team: overdue high-value invoices, failed webhooks and a daily summary. Replaces the stored value. `null` turns every alert off. |
| `team_alerts_config.recipients` | `array of string` | **yes** | Who gets the alerts. Max 10. Required when an alert is enabled. An address that is not a team member gets a confirmation email and no alert until it is confirmed. |
| `team_alerts_config.overdue` | `object` | no | An alert when an unpaid invoice passes its due date and the amount due is at or above the limit for its currency. Checked every hour. An invoice in a currency with no limit gets no alert. |
| `team_alerts_config.webhook_failures` | `object` | no | An hourly alert that lists the webhook endpoints with deliveries we stopped trying to send in the last hour. |
| `team_alerts_config.daily_digest` | `object` | no | A summary at 08:00 business time of the day before: payments collected, payments that failed, invoices in dunning and cards that expire this month or next month. |
| `team_alerts_config.large_grants` | `object` | no | An alert at the time someone gives free credit above `credit_config.grant_limits.<currency>.alert_above_minor`: a wallet top-up of type `granted`, promotional credit or a promotional credit grant. |
| `credit_note_prefix` | `string` | no | A prefix for credit note numbers. |
| `credit_note_next_number` | `integer` | no | The number the next credit note gets. |
| `receipt_prefix` | `string` | no | The prefix of receipt numbers. Default RCPT. |
| `expected_version` | `integer` | no | Optimistic concurrency: current resource_version; 409 on mismatch |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `usage_close_delay_minutes` | `integer` | Extra minutes before a period's usage closes, for apps that buffer events. Usage closes about 6 minutes after the period ends plus this wait, never more than 30 minutes. |
| `object` | `string` | The object type. |
| `id` | `string` | The business's id (biz_…). |
| `name` | `string` | The business's name. |
| `livemode` | `string` | `live` for a live business, `test` for a test business. One of `live`, `test`. |
| `live_business_id` | `string` | On a test business: the id of its live mode. Null on a live business. |
| `test_business_id` | `string` | On a live business: the id of its test mode. Null until test mode is first opened for a business created before test modes existed — POST /v1/businesses/{biz}/test_mode creates it. |
| `default_currency` | `string` | The business's default currency (ISO-4217 code). |
| `currencies` | `array of string` | Currencies this business transacts in; null = unrestricted. |
| `exchange_rates` | `object` | The raw rate map: 1 default_currency = rate × key currency. Kept as numbers for the consumers that already read it; `currency_rates` below is the same rates with their provenance and is the one to prefer. |
| `currency_rates` | `array of object` | Per-currency rate + provenance (one row per configured currency, excluding the business's own default, which is 1 by definition). This is what a currency-settings screen needs: whether the rate is maintained by hand or refreshed from a provider, when the rate being held was PUBLISHED, and why the last refresh failed if it did. |
| `week_start` | `string` | First day of the reporting week. Default `sunday`. One of `sunday`, `monday`. |
| `fiscal_year_start_month` | `integer` | Month (1–12) the fiscal year starts in; default 1 (the calendar year). Fiscal years are named by the year they end in. |
| `status` | `string` | The business's status. |
| `portal_field_config` | `object` | The buyer portal's field matrix, resolved: every key present, tax-locked keys already mandatory. |
| `address_field_locks` | `object` | Address keys the business's live tax setup forces to mandatory on checkout and portal. The settings refuse any other state for them. |
| `team_alerts_config` | `object` | Team alerts. Each alert sends only when it is enabled and `recipients` has at least one address. Mail comes from the platform sender, not from the business mail settings. |
| `created_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the business was created (ISO-8601 UTC). |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `400` | Invalid request body |
| `404` | No such business |
| `409` | resource_version mismatch |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X PATCH "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Brightwater Analytics"
  }'
```
